content.user_title: Deploy Production Apps to Cloud Kubernetes
content.value_statement: Cloud Kubernetes deployments fail when builds, secrets, and runtime settings drift. This skill guides AKS, GKE, and DOKS deployments with CI/CD, Helm, and troubleshooting patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains build-time and runtime variables for Next.js Kubernetes deployments.
Shows GitHub Actions path filters and Docker build platform settings.
Guides Helm deployment with image tags, values overrides, and release commands.
Diagnoses ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff, and CPU architecture mismatches.
References GitOps, observability, RBAC, network policy, HPA, and PDB patterns.
limitations: It does not connect to a cluster or deploy workloads by itself.
Examples use placeholders and require environment-specific review before use.
It does not replace cloud IAM, network, or compliance review.
It focuses on web application deployment, not every Kubernetes workload type.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Cloud Kubernetes Release
use_cases.description: Plan build platforms, Helm values, image tags, and runtime variables before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Create a CI/CD Deployment Flow
use_cases.description: Build a GitHub Actions workflow with path filters, Docker build settings, and Helm release steps.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot a Failed Rollout
use_cases.description: Use Kubernetes events, logs, image errors, and architecture checks to isolate deployment failures.

prompt_templates.title: Check Deployment Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before the first cloud Kubernetes deploy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Kubernetes deployment plan. Check build platform, runtime variables, image tags, Helm values, and missing production steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI/CD Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for GitHub Actions and Helm.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a GitHub Actions pipeline for my app. Include path filters, Docker build settings, image tagging, and Helm deployment steps.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Rollout Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate incident response for a failing Kubernetes release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to troubleshoot my failed rollout. I will provide pod status, events, logs, image tag, cluster architecture, and Helm release details.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of GitOps, observability, security, and resilience.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my production Kubernetes architecture. Evaluate GitOps structure, observability, RBAC, network policy, autoscaling, and disruption handling.

output_examples.input: A user asks why a pod fails with an architecture error after deployment.
output: The response identifies a likely build platform mismatch.
It asks for node architecture and image platform details.
It recommends rebuilding the image for the cluster architecture and redeploying with a fresh tag.

output_examples.input: A team wants a production checklist before deploying a Next.js app to GKE.
output: The response separates build-time public variables from runtime secrets.
It checks Docker platform settings, Helm values, and image tag consistency.
It includes validation steps for logs, events, ingress, and service connectivity.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer asks for production Kubernetes patterns.
output: The response outlines GitOps structure, monitoring, security controls, and resilience settings.
It calls out where placeholders must be replaced with real cluster values.
It recommends validating RBAC, network policy, autoscaling, and disruption budgets before release.

best_practices: Confirm cluster CPU architecture before building container images.
Separate build-time public variables from runtime secrets and configuration.
Use Kubernetes events, pod descriptions, and logs before changing deployment settings.
anti_patterns: Do not assume amd64 images will run on arm64 clusters.
Do not rely on runtime environment variables for Next.js public browser values.
Do not debug Helm values by repeatedly changing production releases without checking rendered output.

faq.question: Which Kubernetes platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on cloud Kubernetes platforms such as AKS, GKE, and DOKS.

faq.question: Can this skill deploy my application automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides deployment guidance, examples, and troubleshooting steps for an AI assistant or engineer to apply.

faq.question: Does it support GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for path filters, Docker build settings, image tagging, and Helm deployment steps.

faq.question: Does it handle Next.js environment variables?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains which variables must be supplied at build time and which belong in runtime configuration.

faq.question: What deployment failures can it help diagnose?
faq.answer: It covers image pull failures, platform mismatches, crash loops, pending pods, Helm parsing issues, and runtime URL problems.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for a security review?
faq.answer: No. Production clusters still need IAM, network, secret, and compliance review by the responsible team.
